C-BROWSER-M1-1-REAL-ENGINE-EVIDENCE-HARD.Title: Browser M1.1 Real Engine Evidence and Hardening: Real Chromium Spike, Confused-Deputy Security, Event Transport, Bounded Query, Complete V1 Operations and Empirical ADR Measurements
C-BROWSER-M1-1-REAL-ENGINE-EVIDENCE-HARD.Summary: Harden Milestone M1.1 deliverables with genuine empirical evidence and strict security enforcement: 1. Execute a real out-of-process Chromium/Edge browser engine spike navigating local HTML fixtures, extracting real Blink AX trees, dispatching real inputs, and testing real renderer process crash containment. 2. Retain the deterministic in-memory provider as a fast reference/test fixture. 3. Eliminate confused-deputy vulnerability by strictly binding InvocationContext resource scope to payload PageId/ContextId/ElementRef. 4. Publish real M0.4 typed browser events post-outcome via Kernel event transport. 5. Implement bounded query snapshots (depth, node count, text length budgets) with explicit truncation markers. 6. Fully wire all advertised v1 capability operations so none returns unsupported. 7. Replace raw filesystem paths in CreateContextRequest with logical profile IDs. 8. Update ADR-BROWSER-ENGINE-V1 to cleanly separate measured empirical numbers from literature assessment.

Goals.Goal: Execute a real out-of-process Chromium engine spike on local HTML fixtures and measure real process/RAM metrics.
Prevent confused-deputy payload spoofing by checking admitted ResourceId against request payload targets.
Publish typed browser events via M0.4 kernel event transport post-outcome.
Bound query/accessibility snapshots with depth and node budget limits.
Fully implement all 8 capability contracts without unsupported operations.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Full production CEF embedding in M1.1 (reserved for M1.2 based on this spike's measurements).
Public internet network crawling or remote web page dependencies.

Constraints.Constraint: BROWSER ENGINE SPIKE MUST EXECUTE A REAL OUT-OF-PROCESS BROWSER ENGINE.
KERNEL ADMITTED RESOURCE SCOPE MUST STRICTLY MATCH PAYLOAD TARGET IDENTITIES.
BROWSER EVENTS ARE OBSERVATIONS PUBLISHED POST-OUTCOME VIA M0.4 TRANSPORT.
QUERY AND ACCESSIBILITY SNAPSHOTS MUST BE BOUNDED TO PREVENT UNBOUNDED IPC ALLOCATIONS.
NO CAPABILITY CONTRACT SHALL BE PUBLISHED WITHOUT FULL CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION.
ARBITRARY HOST FILESYSTEM PATHS SHALL NOT BE PART OF BROWSER CAPABILITY ABI.
KERNEL REMAINS 100% ENGINE-NEUTRAL AND IMPORTS ZERO BROWSER TYPES.

C-BROWSER-M1-1-REAL-ENGINE-EVIDENCE-HARD.VerificationIntent: Verify that real Chromium process executes local navigation, AX extraction, and renderer crash containment on Windows. Verify that confused-deputy resource mismatches are rejected by the capability provider. Verify that browser events are received by kernel event subscribers. Verify query bounding and all v1 operations.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Real out-of-process Chromium process executes local HTML navigation and Blink AX extraction.
Killing renderer process leaves Worldline host process alive and yields typed EngineCrashed error.
Payload targeting PageId different from admitted ResourceId is rejected as ResourceMismatch.
Navigation and crash events are published to kernel event transport and received by subscribers.
Query snapshots respect depth, node count, and text budget bounds with truncation flags.
All 8 contracts and operations are fully implemented without unsupported stubs.
ADR-BROWSER-ENGINE-V1 documents real measured numbers from the Chromium spike.
All CI suites (Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, All) pass.
